page: Amazon Web Services m6a.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a maximum clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The processor includes hardware support for AES, SHA, and AVX instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory consists of 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (286,813.92) and PassMark CPU metrics (114,978.35), complemented by strong memory bandwidth reaching 266.13 GB/sec uncached read and 128.31 GB/sec uncached write. In operational workloads, the platform delivers high throughput, including 175.75 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 73.1 GB/sec in static web serving. Clang compilation and PassMark database operations also place in the upper quartile.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external network-attached storage and standard CPU execution for compute pipelines. Additionally, single-threaded throughput and standard decompression performance remain in the middle tier compared to modern specialized compute chips. However, the high core density and balanced memory allocation offer strong cost efficiency for massive scale-out horizontally parallel services without paying for GPU or high-frequency single-thread premiums.

Given its massive parallelism and large memory footprint, the m6a.48xlarge is well suited for high-concurrency microservices, in-memory caching fleets, distributed database clusters, CI/CD compilation farms, and backend web application serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors and the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores) running at up to 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory across a 4.0 GB per core balance. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps, with zero local storage bundled and no GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier multi-threaded processing and in-memory key-value performance, achieving 175.75 million Redis SET operations per second and high multi-core PassMark ratings. Although single-core throughput remains average and persistence depends strictly on remote network storage, the hardware density provides favorable cost efficiency for heavily threaded workloads. It fits distributed in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, static web fleets, and large multi-tenant container hosts.
